name: What does ADU zoning coordination actually include for a Los Angeles-area permit?

mainEntity.name: What does ADU zoning coordination include when a project is spread across Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, or North Hollywood requirements?

acceptedAnswer.text: ADU zoning coordination is the process of matching a proposed accessory dwelling unit to the correct local rules before drawings are finalized and submitted. In practice, it includes checking the property’s zoning, confirming ADU eligibility, verifying setback and height limits, reviewing lot coverage and open-space constraints, and identifying any special conditions such as hillside, historic, or neighborhood overlay rules. In Los Angeles-area cities, the details can change city by city, so coordination also means making sure the site plan, floor plan, and exterior massing satisfy the specific jurisdiction’s objective standards. Good coordination reduces revisions, delays, and avoidable redesigns. The best next step is to start with the parcel’s zoning, then compare it against the city’s ADU worksheet or zoning handout before budgeting for design and engineering. If there are conflicts, they should be resolved early, not during permit review.
acceptedAnswer.description: ADU zoning coordination means aligning your project with the city’s objective zoning rules before plan submission. It typically covers allowed use, setbacks, height, lot coverage, parking, access, utility placement, historic or overlay constraints, and whether the project can be reviewed ministerially.
